statements.statement: A citizens' petition proposed a Proposition 2½ override; the select board voted not to recommend it and not to place it on the ballot.
The Finance Committee voted to recommend disapproval of the override article, citing insufficient detail on how the money would be spent.
The FY26 omnibus budget total presented to the committee was unchanged from the prior presentation.
A free cash transfer to the schools would occur only if the override fails at the ballot, as a one-time stopgap.
The chair said the $500,000 free-cash infusion is one-time only, and its absence will compound the school budget's problem the following year.
The committee tried to record the net state aid figure for the annual report but the amount was repeated inconsistently in the discussion.
State aid grew at roughly 5.3% annually from FY13 to FY24 according to the draft annual report.
State aid growth slowed to about 1.5% over the last three years, per the draft annual report.
The school department's FY26 budget is expected to eliminate approximately 28 full-time-equivalent positions (39 actual employees), not yet finalized.
Staff contract increases alone were said to total roughly $944,000 for FY26.
Total budgeted staff spending is actually down by about $472,000 between FY25 and FY26 despite contract increases, per the chair's own analysis.
The chair calculated that new revenue plus stated staffing reductions imply an increase of about $4,282,000 (17.21%) that he says needs to be explained.

warnings.condition: the free cash stopgap not being repeated
warnings.prediction: The $500,000 free-cash infusion is one-time only, and its absence will compound the school budget problem next year, driving a future override conversation.
The fire department's shift expansion plan (adding a fourth shift) remains on hold for another year.
